summary: Implement the frozen provider-neutral reconciliation control plane on Task-013 sync primitives with resumable scan modes, bounded durable drift evidence and fail-closed safe remediation actions.

impacts.evidence: Runs, drift records and action receipts are explicit organization/workspace scoped in PostgreSQL and protected by forced RLS.
Reconciliation persists bounded identifiers, fingerprints, status/revision metadata and machine error codes only; no remote payload bodies, credentials or raw errors.
Task 014 adds no public HTTP endpoint; scheduled and on-demand callers use an internal platform capability.
No new EventBus schema is introduced. Remediation adapters retain ownership of their existing domain events.
Connector SDK v1 interfaces are unchanged; scanning and remediation are host-side ports.
Expand migration 000025 adds resumable runs, immutable drift evidence and append-only action receipts with forced RLS.
Auto-fix is permitted only for unambiguous mapping creation or source-of-truth/direction-authorized content/status repair. Ambiguous mapping and health drift fail closed.
Approval is an explicit remediation action; external approval integration is called with deterministic idempotency evidence rather than bypassed.
Immutable drift and action receipts preserve machine-readable reconciliation evidence without replacing Audit/Data Lineage.
Deterministic drift IDs suppress page replay duplicates, persisted cursor enables resume, and deterministic action keys protect external remediation retries.
Notification/remediation delivery occurs through a host action executor and does not bypass Task-063 webhook infrastructure.
Runs expose scanned/drift counts and detect stale remote observation timestamps; Task 066 later defines production thresholds and load profiles.
Disable reconciliation scheduling to stop new work. Expand-only evidence is retained; completed runs and action history are immutable.
Tests cover drift classes, safe/unsafe remediation, stale health, interrupted-run resume and machine-code-only action failures.
